claim_policy: Additive bibliography refresh; dates are publication dates, not the date this repository discovered a paper. No 98% claim has been identified or reproduced.

papers.summary: DDO introduces a decoy signal that can mislead contrastive refusal-direction estimators. A high separation score is therefore insufficient evidence that a direction causally controls refusal.
papers.implication: Pair localization with interventions and held-out evaluation; test robustness to estimator failure.
papers.title: Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration

papers.scope: Skill-merged models; static and adaptive evaluation
papers.summary: SkillSafe-Bench compares static refusal, adaptive robustness, and retained skills. A model that passes static screening can still behave differently under adaptive evaluation.
papers.implication: Track utility and robustness separately from a single refusal percentage.
papers.title: When Skills Meet Safety: Benchmarking and Characterizing the Adaptive Jailbreak Robustness of Skill-Merged LLMs

papers.summary: Refusal phrases can act as misleading shortcuts for guard classifiers. Sparse masking reduces this shortcut in the studied models without requiring full retraining.
papers.implication: A lexical refusal count is a screening metric, not a harmfulness judge or attack-success measure.
papers.title: When Refusal Looks Safe: The Refusal-Cue Shortcut in Safety Guard Models

papers.summary: ToolAlignBench studies conflicts between safety-trained values and deployment instructions in tool-using agents. It evaluates behavior beyond answer-level refusal.
papers.implication: Test tool protocol, instruction adherence, and unintended actions before deploying an edited agent.
papers.title: ToolAlignBench: Investigating Alignment Conflicts in Tool-Calling Enabled LLMs

papers.summary: The study links training curricula to separable circuits and the selectivity of subsequent fine-tuning. Its controlled tasks help explain why identical update budgets can behave differently across models.
papers.implication: Treat localization as model- and training-dependent rather than assuming universal safety layers.
papers.title: Pretraining Curricula Enable Selective Fine-tuning

papers.summary: SafeVec extracts reference refusal directions and uses stable layer windows to calculate the Refusal Alignment Score. Its calibrated representation score is not interchangeable with a raw separation norm.
papers.implication: Keep representation diagnostics, calibration, and output-level evaluation distinct.
papers.title: RAS: Measuring LLM Safety Through Refusal Alignment

papers.summary: TF-RefusalBench measures legitimate criminal-law tasks across languages. Refusal, disclaimers, and task faithfulness are evaluated separately in an applied setting.
papers.implication: Include benign sensitive-domain tasks and language coverage, with explicit limits on the test set.
papers.title: Measuring & Mitigating Over-Alignment for LLMs in Multilingual Criminal Law Courts

papers.scope: Harmfulness and refusal under adversarial fine-tuning
papers.summary: The work studies how harmfulness and refusal geometry become coupled or decoupled during training. A checkpoint's current output behavior does not fully describe its internal changes.
papers.implication: Report a baseline, a bounded edit footprint, and multiple behavioral axes together.
papers.title: From Refusal Geometry to Safety Geometry: Harmfulness--Refusal Coupling under Dynamic Adversarial Fine-Tuning

papers.summary: LoMC localizes an editable support before combining correction directions, then confines the weight update to that support. Its MoE experiments do not establish the same result on dense MiniCPM5.
papers.implication: Separate where to edit from how to edit; account for edited tensors and parameters explicitly.
papers.title: LoMC: Localized Multidirectional Correction for Refusal Suppression in Routed Foundation Models

papers.summary: This study tests whether defenses against harmful fine-tuning also withstand simpler inference and weight interventions. It introduces abliteration-resistant tuning as an additional defense.
papers.implication: Evaluate attack families beyond the one used during training; retain a defense comparison.
papers.title: Open-Weight LLM Fine-Tuning Defenses are Susceptible to Simple Attacks

papers.scope: Comparison of SFT, RLVR, and refusal-feature ablation
papers.summary: Matched harmful compliance can hide different capability losses, representation changes, and self-audit behavior. Different intervention mechanisms should not be collapsed into one method label.
papers.implication: Distinguish direct projection from gradient-based fine-tuning in commands, manifests, and results.
papers.title: Behind Harmful Compliance: Behavioral and Mechanistic Divergence Across LLM Jailbreaks

papers.summary: This controlled study reports a failed topic-matched contrast construction despite success with an unmatched contrast on the tested model. A more carefully matched dataset is not automatically a better causal estimator.
papers.implication: Record contrast construction and failure cases; do not pick layers using held-out test outcomes.
papers.title: On the Failure of Topic-Matched Contrast Baselines in Multi-Directional Refusal Abliteration

papers.summary: NeST probes safety-relevant neurons and learns shared cluster updates while freezing other parameters. It strengthens safety; it is not evidence for the recalled refusal-removal percentage.
papers.implication: Distinguish neuron selection from layer selection and from whole-tensor fine-tuning.
papers.title: NeST: Neuron Selective Tuning for LLM Safety

papers.summary: Gabliteration studies adaptive multidirectional projections and regularized layer selection. It is included as a previously missing methodological connection, not as a September publication.
papers.implication: Compare sparse support and multiple directions with the original single-direction baseline.
papers.title: Gabliteration: Adaptive Multi-Directional Neural Weight Modification for Selective Behavioral Alteration in Large Language Models
